title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Treasury yields surged Wednesday - the 10-year hit ~5.11%-5.13%, its highest since 2007 - after a weak 5-year auction and strong US PMI data; S&P 500 fell 0.8% to 7,706, Nasdaq lost 1.1% to 26,936, Dow shed 352 pts (-0.7%).
Markets: Brent crude snapped a 5-session losing streak, jumping ~4% to $103/bbl on uncertainty over US-Iran talks at the UN and worries about a potential US diesel export ban hitting European supply.
Markets: October rate-hike odds jumped to ~70% (from 55% a day earlier) per CME FedWatch, after Fed Governor Michael Barr said he expects further increases; the Fed hiked to 3.75%-4.00% last week.
Companies: McDonald's fell nearly 5% after unveiling an $8.5B plan to help franchisees invest in equipment and operations to keep pace with fast-food rivals.
Companies: Alphabet (-3%) and Amazon (-1.9%) slid amid renewed scrutiny of AI-hyperscaler debt issuance and competitive threat from Meta's new 'Muse' AI agent.
Companies: IonQ jumped 12% after announcing the industry's first real-time quantum error decoder for quantum error correction.

Macro/Policy: Trump and Xi Jinping meet at the White House today for a summit centered on trade, technology and Taiwan; the US-China trade truce was extended two months but little concrete progress is expected.
Macro/Policy: Darden Restaurants and Costco report earnings today; new-home sales data and the Kansas City Fed's September survey are due; Philadelphia Fed's Anna Paulson (FOMC voter) speaks.
